title: Change an electric toothbrush's head: hold the handle, pull the worn head off and push a new one on
instruction: Change the electric toothbrush's brush head: hold the toothbrush's handle with one hand. With the other, pull the worn brush head straight off its metal shaft and drop it in the bin, then take the new brush head from its pack and push it straight onto the shaft, all the way on. Then let go of both and take both arms back to where they started.
context: Electric toothbrush heads are swapped every few months, a small chore of daily life that people who have lost the use of a hand need help with: the head is a tight push fit on its shaft, so the handle has to be held while the head is pulled off and pushed on.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) A dark grey granite bathroom counter top 1 cm thick, from 17 to 48 cm forward and from 23 cm right to 20 cm left of the centre line, fixed. (2) Lying on its back on the counter, an electric toothbrush (0.14 kg): a white plastic handle 17 cm long and 2.6 cm across with a flat back, a blue band and a blue power button, its steel drive shaft (4.4 mm across, 2.4 cm long) pointing forward; the handle's middle is 28 cm forward, 0.5 cm right of the centre line. (3) On the shaft, a worn round brush head (10 g): a dark blue collar 1.6 cm across, a white neck 1.1 cm across and 5.2 cm long and a round head 1.9 cm across with yellowed, splayed bristles facing up. It sits on the shaft with a press fit. (4) A new brush head, the same with white and blue bristles, lying in its open blister pack (a blue card 10 x 5 cm with clear cradles) 25.5 cm forward and 14 cm right of the centre line, its neck pointing forward, level with the shaft. (5) A white pedal bin 9 cm across and 8.5 cm tall, 40.5 cm forward and 17.5 cm right of the centre line, fixed. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Judged at the end of the trial. A head slides along the shaft only when pushed or pulled with more than about 3 N (a press fit), and stays where it is left; the worn head is off once pulled out past the shaft's end. A new head pushed onto the shaft's end (within 1 cm of its axis and 15 degrees of its line) catches on it; it is all the way on when its base is within 3 mm of the shaft's base. 1.0: the new head all the way on, the worn head in the bin and both arms back where they started (each gripper's fingertip centre within 5 cm of its start); 0.5: the new head all the way on; 0.25: the worn head off the shaft; else 0.0. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held for 1 s with the toothbrush and the new head still.
reset_notes: Push the worn head back onto the shaft, put the new head back in its pack and lay the toothbrush on its back in its place.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz control). Simplified: the press fit is a joint that keeps a head on the shaft's axis and lets it slide along it only against about 3 N, as the scoring describes; the heads do not collide with the handle. The toothbrush's handle has a flat back so it lies still. Cameras 1280 x 704 (Dream-1 sees 320 x 176).
